Have you run `dotnet nuget add source <my_local_source> --name MyLocalNugetSource` to add the custom-built SDK to the local NuGet source?
https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/engine_details/development/compiling/compiling_with_dotnet.html#nuget-packages

> Have you run `dotnet nuget add source --name MyLocalNugetSource` to add the custom-built SDK to the local NuGet source? https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/engine_details/development/compiling/compiling_with_dotnet.html#nuget-packages I believe so. Does this look right? I see it's listing Godot 4.2.2 I don't see anything related to a dotnet 4.8.0-dev nor 4.8.0-dev.1

The editor binary automatically changes the Godot .NET SDK version to the one that matches the editor, which in this case is `4.8.0-dev`. Changing it manually to `4.8.0-dev.1` is not correct, that version is only supported for the official release [Godot 4.8 dev 1](https://godotengine.org/article/dev-snapshot-godot-4-8-dev-1/) and may cause issues with your custom build.

The package version `4.8.0-dev` is a custom build, it doesn't have the revision number we add at the end for official releases. This means, as @scgm0 mentioned, that you need to look at the build documentation and make sure you are:
1. Building the engine and the .NET packages correctly.
2. Ensuring the .NET packages are added to a custom NuGet feed source.
3. Ensuring the NuGet feed source with the built packages is registered and enabled.

It looks like you built the engine and have configured the NuGet feed source, but you are missing adding the .NET packages to the NuGet feed source. You either forgot to build the .NET packages (did you run the `build_assemblies.py` script?), didn't use the `--push-nupkgs-local` flag, or used the flag incorrectly.

Make sure you run the `build_assemblies.py` script after building the engine, and then use the `--push-nupkgs-local` flag pointing at your `MyLocalNugetSource` directory or copy the packages manually. Remember that the flag expects the absolute path to the `MyLocalNuGetSource` directory. All of these steps are already documented in the link that @scgm0 shared earlier: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/engine_details/development/compiling/compiling_with_dotnet.html#nuget-packages

I'll close this since it's not an engine issue, but feel free to reopen if any of the documented steps fail.
